crucialFeats: Two-finger push-ups and extreme body control.
Creation of Jeet Kune Do by combining styles.

dossier.advantage: Extremely trained body and inhuman speed. He possesses total muscle control, allowing him to deliver powerful strikes from zero distance.
dossier.mentality: Instant adaptation and instinctive precision. He reads the opponent's intentions in a fraction of a second, striking where the defense is weakest.
dossier.style: Masterful synthesis of Jeet Kune Do. Bruce Lee combines boxing, fencing, and Wing Chun into one fluid system, eliminating unnecessary movements.

fighterA.name: Bruce Lee

powers: Elite human speed, reflexes, coordination, and precision striking.
tools: JKD interception timing, low kicks, rhythm disruption, and cross-style adaptation.
Nunchaku and staff (in street scenarios), extreme power of the one-inch punch.
weaknesses: Significant size and reach deficit versus heavyweight specialists.
Lack of proven experience taking hits from professional heavyweight boxers.

crucialFeats: Wins his first world title at age 22.
Defeated 21 champions or heavyweight title challengers.

dossier.advantage: Heavyweight durability and ring intelligence. He can take a punch, but his true strength lies in avoiding them and dictating the fight's pace.
dossier.mentality: A charismatic showman with a will of steel. He provokes the opponent to throw them off balance and methodically break their confidence.
dossier.quote: Float like a butterfly, sting like a bee.
dossier.style: Masterful control of distance and rhythm. He uses legendary footwork and a quick command of the ring to frustrate enemies.

fighterB.name: Muhammad Ali

powers: Elite heavyweight boxing speed, timing, durability, and ring IQ.
tools: Jab control, footwork, defensive movement, clinch management, and pacing control.
Ability to survive punishing rounds and 'rope-a-dope' - exhausting the opponent.
weaknesses: Primarily boxing-centric toolkit compared with broad open-rule combat sets.
Vulnerability to low kicks and joint attacks that boxing does not account for.

battle-dynamics.phase_1: Bruce Lee attempts to shock Ali with speed, but the boxing geography of the ring favors the heavyweight champion.
battle-dynamics.phase_2: Ali establishes the jab. Every time Bruce enters the range, he is scored upon by Ali, who controls the rhythm.
battle-dynamics.phase_3: Bruce's fatigue and Ali's mass advantage close the fight. Ali wins on points or by technical knockout.
battle-dynamics.analysis: In the ring, Ali is unbeatable for Bruce. The mass and reach difference is simply too vast.
battle-dynamics.s2_phase_1: Bruce Lee takes advantage of the lack of barriers and low kicks to the knees. Ali must suddenly adapt to unknown attack angles.
battle-dynamics.s2_phase_2: The fight becomes chaotic. Bruce uses elbows and interceptions, neutralizing Ali's boxing rhythm.
battle-dynamics.s2_phase_3: Ali still has the power edge, but the lack of gloves makes Bruce's strikes to vital points decisive.
battle-dynamics.s2_analysis: The street levels the playing field, giving Bruce access to the full Jeet Kune Do arsenal.
battle-dynamics.s3_phase_1: Death rules in the ring are a sentence for the lighter fighter. Ali does not need to conserve energy for rounds.
battle-dynamics.s3_phase_2: Bruce desperately tries to land a lethal blow, but Ali simply 'crushes' him with his weight in the clinch.
battle-dynamics.s3_phase_3: Pure physics. Ali ends the fight with a brutal knockout that Bruce's body cannot survive.
battle-dynamics.s3_analysis: Death rules in the ring reward physical power and Ali's scale.
battle-dynamics.s4_phase_1: Bruce Lee strikes to kill in the first second. Kicks to the groin and eyes – zero sportsmanship.
battle-dynamics.s4_phase_2: Ali, wounded and enraged, tries to grab Bruce. Every punch Ali lands is like a hammer strike.
battle-dynamics.s4_phase_3: A war of attrition. Bruce Lee wins through mobility, but both emerge tragically mangled.
battle-dynamics.s4_analysis: The bloodiest scenario, where Bruce's speed and dirty techniques give him the edge.

fight-simulation.opening: Bruce Lee attempts to set the pace, but Ali 'floats like a butterfly' around him.
fight-simulation.mid_fight: Ali sets the range with a left jab, not allowing Bruce to enter with a combination.
fight-simulation.late_fight: Ali's reach advantage becomes an impenetrable wall.
fight-simulation.end_condition: Ali's victory by technical knockout in the late phase.
fight-simulation.phase_1_event: Bruce performs a series of lightning-fast dodges, but Ali calmly keeps him at range with the jab.
fight-simulation.phase_2_event: Ali moves in circles, forcing Bruce into constant footwork that tires him.
fight-simulation.phase_2_branch_a: Bruce finds a gap and lands a single strike.
fight-simulation.phase_2_branch_b: Ali counters with a double jab, weakening Bruce's guard.
fight-simulation.phase_3_event: Ali moves to the offensive, raining combinations that cannot be blocked by hands.
fight-simulation.phase_3_branch_a: Bruce hits the canvas after a series of hooks.
fight-simulation.phase_3_branch_b: The referee stops the fight due to a cut on Bruce.
fight-simulation.s2_phase_1_event: Bruce attacks Ali's legs with low side kicks, destroying his footwork.
fight-simulation.s2_phase_2_event: Rapid exchanges without gloves. Every one of Bruce's strikes is precisely aimed at joints.
fight-simulation.s2_phase_2_branch_a: Ali is immobilized by knee pain.
fight-simulation.s2_phase_2_branch_b: Ali catches Bruce in a clinch and uses his mass.
fight-simulation.s2_phase_3_event: Bruce closes the distance to zero and strikes with full force into Ali's chest.
fight-simulation.s2_phase_3_branch_a: Ali loses his breath and falls to his knees.
fight-simulation.s2_phase_3_branch_b: Ali pushes Bruce away but loses control of the fight.
fight-simulation.s2_end_condition: Bruce's victory through Ali's inability to continue the fight.
fight-simulation.s3_phase_1_event: Ali ignores technical aspects and strives to physically smother the opponent.
fight-simulation.s3_phase_2_event: Every one of Ali's punches is lethal. Bruce must be perfect not to die on the spot.
fight-simulation.s3_phase_2_branch_a: Ali breaks Bruce's ribs with a single body shot.
fight-simulation.s3_phase_2_branch_b: Bruce tries desperately to counter to the eyes.
fight-simulation.s3_phase_3_event: Ali strikes with all his weight into Bruce's jaw. It's over.
fight-simulation.s3_end_condition: Ali's total dominance through physical advantage.
fight-simulation.s4_phase_1_event: Bruce attacks Ali's throat and eyes, aiming to end the Titan's life as quickly as possible.
fight-simulation.s4_phase_2_event: Ali is bleeding but still pressing forward. Bruce must move faster than ever.
fight-simulation.s4_phase_2_branch_a: Bruce avoids a massive haymaker and counters to the temple.
fight-simulation.s4_phase_2_branch_b: Ali grabs Bruce's clothes and pulls him in.
fight-simulation.s4_phase_3_event: Bruce executes a series of strikes to the solar plexus and larynx.
fight-simulation.s4_phase_3_branch_a: Ali falls dead, unable to catch his breath.
fight-simulation.s4_phase_3_branch_b: Both fall from exhaustion and wounds.
fight-simulation.s4_end_condition: Bruce Lee's victory through ruthless precision.

final-summary.line_1: This is a clash of precision versus power. Bruce Lee has speed Ali has never encountered, but Ali has a scale Bruce cannot ignore.
final-summary.line_2: In the ring, the rules and Ali's mass give him a nearly certain victory. On the street, where Bruce can use his full arsenal, the odds level out.
final-summary.line_3: Ultimately, it is a fight of whether one perfect Bruce strike can topple a man who survived 15 rounds with the world's strongest boxers.
final-summary.winner: Muhammad Ali in the ring, Bruce Lee on the street.
final-summary.quote: “I fear not the man who has practiced 10,000 kicks once, but I fear the man who has practiced one kick 10,000 times... unless that man is Muhammad Ali.”

tactical-board.lane: Bruce must keep the fight dirty and chaotic. Ali wins if he imposes boxing distance.
tactical-board.subtitle: Artist versus Boxer

verdict-matrix.subtitle: Zero variables affecting the outcome
verdict-matrix.verdict: Muhammad Ali 10/10. While the legend of Bruce Lee is fascinating, real-world physics and combat facts are ruthless. Ali possessed approximately a 36kg weight advantage, a massive reach advantage (hands over legs), and a proven durability against strikes Bruce never had to endure. In a clash between a professional heavyweight world champion and a martial artist several weight classes lighter, every scenario ends in a swift and brutal knockout in Ali's favor.

x-factor.implication: This is why Ali wins unquestionably in the ring, while on the street, Bruce becomes a lethal threat.
x-factor.mechanics: Ali possesses a chin of steel and heavyweight mass. Bruce must strike perfectly at points muscles do not protect.
x-factor.psychology: Ali wants to toy with the opponent. Bruce is pure, focused professionalism.
x-factor.example: Bruce lands a perfect side kick to Ali's knee. On the street, it's the end of the fight. In the ring, Ali might survive through adrenaline and the clinch.
x-factor.question: Is Bruce's speed enough to avoid every Ali jab for the entire fight?
